caseStudy: School and club sports day on a 67.6 x 21 m roof, 5 load cases, 16 bays

assumptions: Screening model, not a structural verification or a vibration design.

Crowds: an agent simulation of the day "School and club sports day" (06:00 to 23:00, fixed random seed). People arrive at the entries, walk in straight lines at 1.3 m/s (circulation paths are not followed), settle on their court, play area or garden and wander about it, and leave. How full each piece is each hour (a share of its players, seats or garden visitors) is the author's schedule. A person weighs 90 kg.

Weather: each case is a characteristic combination, without partial safety factors. Permanent load: build-ups dry, at field capacity (where the storm starts) or wet, as the case says; the static analysis's saturated weight is the envelope of all of them.

Rain: the cloudburst of the rain analysis (108 mm/h for 10 min) through each zone's own column, from field capacity. Snow: DIN EN 1991-1-3/NA ground load for zone 2 at 100 m, times 0.8 (flat roof); no drifting or sliding. Wind: the wind analysis's roof zones and peak pressure, the direction that lifts a bay most. Event in winter: EN 1990 combination values 0.7 (crowd) and 0.5 (snow).

Resonance: each bay is one simply supported strip along its long span, depth span/25 (0.2 to 0.6 m, no slab thickness was given), E = 30 GPa, damping 0.03; the natural frequency is ESTIMATED from that (good to about 25%), and the response is the worst over that band. The crowd drives the harmonics of its rhythm with the dynamic load factors of a half-sine pulse train (jumping: contact ratio 1/3 gives 1.8, 1.29, 0.67; Bachmann and Ammann) or walking 0.4, 0.1, 0.1; participants add as sync x N + (1 - sync) x sqrt(N) with sync 0 (walking), 0.2 (court play), 0.6 (event). A jumping event is 0.25 people per m2 on the courts and play areas only (planted gardens carry walkers, not a jumping crowd). Steady-state response; acceleration limits 0.02 g (walking) and 0.05 g (rhythmic activities): see the inputs below for whose they are.
Capacity: 8 kN/m2 (a PLACEHOLDER: enter the engineer's figure).

Input - Deck capacity: 8 kN/m2, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (PLACEHOLDER for a project figure). No code value: it is the structural engineer's figure for the deck (characteristic permanent + imposed load per m2).

Input - Deck's first natural frequency: estimated, 4.5 to 9.2 Hz, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (ESTIMATED from the model). The first vertical mode from the engineer's structural model (DIN EN 1990/NA, vibration serviceability).
Input - Snow load zone: zone 2, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (the author's assumption). DIN EN 1991-1-3/NA: the German snow load zone map (zones 1, 1a, 2, 2a, 3).
Input - Site altitude: 100 m, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (the author's assumption). DIN EN 1991-1-3/NA: the ground snow load rises with the altitude above sea level in every zone.
Input - Use over the day: school and club sports day, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (the author's assumption). Not defined by any standard: the operator's booking plan is the right source.

Input - Comfort limit, walking: 0.02 g, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (the author's assumption). No DIN table. Published guidance (SCI P354, CCIP-016, ISO 10137) ranges from about 0.5% g for offices upward with the use.

Input - Comfort limit, rhythmic activity: 0.05 g, built-in value, NOT CONFIRMED (the author's assumption). SCI P354 gives about 3% g for gymnasia; ISO 10137 and CCIP-016 give the framework. No DIN table.

recommendations.text: The roof is busiest at 12:03 with about 40 people (35 kN); Bay 8.1 is the most crowded bay, 0.27 people per m2 at 12:53, 9% of what the deck is designed for there.

The crowd is 1% of the load at its busiest: it moves the load's centre by at most 0.13% (toward the top, at 12:03), on top of the 18.1% the permanent load already has. The weight of the build-ups decides the balance, not the people.
3 bays exceed the deck capacity in some weather: Bay 8.1 reaches 152% in "Event in winter" (the static design case gives 188%). Lighten what stands there or have the deck checked.
A 108 mm/h cloudburst adds up to 150 kN of water to the build-ups by minute 10 (4590 kN in all; saturated: 4826 kN).
The snow load uses an ASSUMED snow zone (2) and an ASSUMED altitude of 100 m: enter the site's snow zone and altitude in the Site conditions tab. sk = 0.85 kN/m2.

Bay 4.2 reaches 0.13 g under jumping event (comfort limit 0.05 g): harmonic 2 of a 2.7 Hz rhythm meets the deck at 6.6 Hz. Only a deck above 8.4 Hz (harmonic 3 of the fastest rhythm; stiffness about x1.6) is clear of the crowd's harmonics; otherwise more damping, or keeping rhythmic events off this bay.
The deck's frequency is an ESTIMATE from the spans (4.5 to 9.2 Hz, good to about 25%). Enter the structural engineer's first natural frequency in the Structure inputs tab before relying on this.
The deck capacity (8 kN/m2) is a placeholder: enter the structural engineer's figure.
